fixes.explanation: Jesus tells Sardis, “you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead.” A reputation is what a church is known for, and for Sardis that was being alive. I've seen cookies that looked perfect on the cooling rack and were still doughy inside, so I know how looks can fool you. Jesus sees past the outside.

Generosity never comes up in Jesus' words to Sardis. The reputation He names is being alive. He says He knows their deeds, and then He names what they're known for. Nice guess, friend, but the text only gives us the one word.

Poor isn't the word Jesus uses for Sardis. What He says is “you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead.” He sets how they look right next to how they really are, and that gap is the whole problem. Think of a cookie box that looks gorgeous on the outside and has nothing in it. The word to hold onto is dead.

Jesus never tells Sardis to leave town. He says, “Wake up and strengthen what remains…” He's speaking to the church, and the command is to wake up and strengthen what's left. A suitcase isn't part of that.

Jesus says, “If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief…” He adds that they “will not know the hour” when He comes (Revelation 3:3). That's the point of the picture. It's a warning, and it comes with a way to be ready: wake up.

Jesus does say it. “But you do have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and because they are worthy, they will walk with Me in white.” The letter says there are a few, though it doesn't name them. The promise to them is that they will walk with Him.

Jesus says, “What He opens no one can shut, and what He shuts no one can open.” That's a lot of power in a single key. Nobody can slam what He opens. I spent years in the back of a drawer that someone else shut, so I notice that line.
That's not what Jesus says. He says, “What He opens no one can shut, and what He shuts no one can open.” Nothing in the verse mentions night or closing time. What He opens, no one can shut.

Spoken isn't the word Jesus uses. He says they “have not denied My name,” and that's a different thing from speaking it. Denying is turning away from the name when it costs you something. Jesus says that about a church with only a little strength.

Warns isn't the word in this verse. Jesus says, “…and they will know that I love you.” Those liars come to know something about the church in Philadelphia, and it's not a warning. It's that He loves them. Good guess, friend, but the word is loves.
